questions.stem: How many rupees did Kiran have at the start?
questions.explanation: Work backwards. Before round 3, Kiran and Leela had half of 48, that is 24 each, and Manav had 48 + 24 + 24 = 96. Before round 2, Kiran had 12 and Manav 48, and Leela had 24 + 12 + 48 = 84. Before round 1, Leela had 42 and Manav 24, and Kiran had 12 + 42 + 24 = 78. Kiran started with Rs 78.

questions.stem: How many rupees did Leela have at the start?
questions.explanation: Work backwards. Before round 3, Kiran and Leela had half of 48, that is 24 each, and Manav had 48 + 24 + 24 = 96. Before round 2, Kiran had 12 and Manav 48, and Leela had 24 + 12 + 48 = 84. Before round 1, Leela had 42 and Manav 24, and Kiran had 12 + 42 + 24 = 78. Leela started with Rs 42.

questions.stem: How many rupees did Manav have at the end of round 2?
questions.explanation: Work backwards. Before round 3, Kiran and Leela had half of 48, that is 24 each, and Manav had 48 + 24 + 24 = 96. Before round 2, Kiran had 12 and Manav 48, and Leela had 24 + 12 + 48 = 84. Before round 1, Leela had 42 and Manav 24, and Kiran had 12 + 42 + 24 = 78. At the end of round 2 (just before round 3) Manav had Rs 96.

questions.stem: Who held the most money at the end of round 1?
options: Leela
Kiran
Manav
Kiran and Manav equally
questions.explanation: Work backwards. Before round 3, Kiran and Leela had half of 48, that is 24 each, and Manav had 48 + 24 + 24 = 96. Before round 2, Kiran had 12 and Manav 48, and Leela had 24 + 12 + 48 = 84. Before round 1, Leela had 42 and Manav 24, and Kiran had 12 + 42 + 24 = 78. After round 1 the holdings were Kiran 12, Leela 84 and Manav 48, so Leela held the most.

questions.stem: Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% are equal to a single discount of what percentage?
questions.explanation: After 20% off, 80 remains of 100; 10% off that leaves 72. The single discount is 28%, not 30%, because the second discount is taken on a smaller price.

questions.stem: Pipe A fills a tank in 12 hours and pipe B in 20 hours, while pipe C empties the full tank in 30 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, how many hours does it take to fill?
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/20 - 1/30 = (5 + 3 - 2)/60 = 6/60 of the tank an hour, so it fills in 10 hours. Ignoring C gives 7.5 hours.

questions.stem: A boat's speed in still water is 18 km/h and the stream flows at 2 km/h. How many hours does the boat take to go 40 km downstream and come back?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed is 20 km/h and upstream 16 km/h, so the trip takes 40/20 + 40/16 = 2 + 2.5 = 4.5 hours.

questions.stem: The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a sum for 2 years at 10% a year is Rs 150. What is the sum, in rupees?
questions.explanation: For 2 years the difference is the interest on the first year's interest: P x (10/100)^2 = P/100. So P/100 = 150 and P = 15,000.

questions.stem: Section A has 30 students with an average mark of 62 and section B has 50 students with an average of 70. What is the average mark of all 80 students?
questions.explanation: Total marks = 30 x 62 + 50 x 70 = 1,860 + 3,500 = 5,360, and 5,360/80 = 67. The simple average of 62 and 70 is 66, which ignores that B is larger.

questions.stem: How many kilograms of rice costing Rs 42 per kg must be mixed with 30 kg of rice costing Rs 54 per kg so that the mixture costs Rs 50 per kg?
questions.explanation: The cheaper rice is 8 below the mixture price and the dearer 4 above it, so the quantities are in the ratio 4 : 8 = 1 : 2. With 30 kg of the dearer rice, 15 kg of the cheaper one is needed.

questions.stem: Two cars 300 km apart set off towards each other at 9:00 a.m., one at 55 km/h and the other at 45 km/h. At what time do they meet?
options: 12:00 noon
questions.explanation: Moving towards each other, they close the gap at 55 + 45 = 100 km/h, so they meet after 300/100 = 3 hours, at noon.

questions.stem: A town's population rises by 10% in one year and falls by 10% the next. Compared with the start, the population:
options: is unchanged
rises by 1%
falls by 2%
falls by 1%
questions.explanation: 100 becomes 110, then 110 - 11 = 99: a net fall of 1%. The 10% fall is taken on the larger figure, so it outweighs the rise.

questions.stem: The equation $x^2 + kx + 16 = 0$ has two equal roots, and $k$ is positive. What is $k$?
questions.explanation: Equal roots need a zero discriminant: $k^2 - 4 \times 16 = 0$, so $k^2 = 64$ and, since $k$ is positive, $k = 8$.

questions.stem: What is the minimum value of $f(x) = x^2 - 4x$?
questions.explanation: Completing the square, $x^2 - 4x = (x - 2)^2 - 4$, which is smallest, -4, when $x = 2$.

questions.stem: The sum of two numbers is 52 and their difference is 14. What is the larger number?
questions.explanation: Adding the two equations gives twice the larger number: 52 + 14 = 66, so the larger is 33 and the smaller 19.

questions.stem: The sum of the first $n$ odd natural numbers is 400. What is $n$?
questions.explanation: The first $n$ odd numbers add up to $n^2$, so $n^2 = 400$ and $n = 20$.

questions.stem: If $2^{x + 1} = 64$, what is the value of $3^{x - 1}$?
Which values of $x$ satisfy $x^2 - 7x + 12 < 0$?
options: $x > 4$ only
questions.explanation: $x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x - 3)(x - 4)$, which is negative only between its roots, so $3 < x < 4$. Outside the roots the product is positive.

questions.stem: Given that $\log_{10} 2 = 0.301$, how many digits does $2^{50}$ have?
What is the area of an equilateral triangle with sides of 12 cm, in sq cm?
questions.explanation: Area = (√3/4) x side^2 = (√3/4) x 144 = 36√3. Its height is 6√3, and half of 12 x 6√3 is again 36√3.

questions.stem: Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150 degrees. How many sides does it have?
questions.explanation: Each exterior angle is 180 - 150 = 30 degrees, and the exterior angles of any polygon add up to 360, so there are 360/30 = 12 sides.

questions.stem: A cylinder has a radius of 7 cm and a height of 15 cm. Taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$, what is its volume in cubic cm?
questions.explanation: Volume = $\pi r^2 h = \frac{22}{7} \times 49 \times 15 = 2310$ cubic cm.

questions.stem: Which is the equation of the straight line through the points (1, 2) and (3, 8)?
options: y = 2x
questions.explanation: The slope is (8 - 2)/(3 - 1) = 3. Putting (1, 2) into y = 3x + c gives c = -1. Check with (3, 8): 9 - 1 = 8.

questions.stem: The HCF of two numbers is 15 and their LCM is 450. If one of them is 90, what is the other?
questions.explanation: For two numbers, HCF x LCM = product, so the other is 15 x 450 / 90 = 75. Check: HCF(90, 75) = 15 and LCM = 450.

questions.stem: What is the units digit of $3^{47}$?
questions.explanation: Units digits of powers of 3 repeat 3, 9, 7, 1. Since 47 leaves remainder 3 on division by 4, the units digit is the third in the cycle, 7.

questions.stem: Two fair dice are thrown. What is the probability that the numbers shown add up to 8?
questions.explanation: The pairs (2, 6), (3, 5), (4, 4), (5, 3) and (6, 2) give 8: 5 of the 36 equally likely outcomes. A total of 7 would have 6 ways, 1/6.

questions.stem: The passage argues that note-taking helps memory mainly because it:
options: forces the writer to decide what matters
lets the writer copy a lecture word for word
gives the writer a record to look up later
keeps the writer's hands busy during a lecture
questions.explanation: The author calls the record "one use" and says "the less obvious use" is that writing a good note "forces the writer to decide what matters."

questions.stem: What does the author say about students who copy a lecture word for word?
options: They cannot keep up with a fast speaker
They are usually the ones who use a pen
They remember more than students who summarise
They gain a full record but little understanding
questions.explanation: The second paragraph: such a student "gains a complete record and very little understanding."

questions.stem: The author's position on laptops in lectures is that:
options: the habit of copying is the problem, not the device
laptops should be banned because they prevent learning
teachers should decide which students may use them
laptops are always better than pens for taking notes
questions.explanation: The third paragraph says "the problem is not the machine but the habit it encourages"; a laptop user who writes in their own words gains the same benefit.

questions.stem: According to the last paragraph, notes can harm learning when they:
options: contain too many summaries and too few quotations
are kept too long after the examination is over
make us believe work is done because words are on the page
are written by hand rather than typed on a keyboard
questions.explanation: The passage ends: notes harm "when they let us believe the work has been done because the words are safely on the page."

questions.stem: According to the passage, both common predictions about automated crafts share the assumption that:
options: crafts that survive will become luxuries for the rich
customers prefer handmade goods to machine-made ones
machines will always do a task better than people do
the craft is the same as the task the machine takes over
questions.explanation: The first paragraph says both predictions "share a mistaken assumption: that the craft is the same thing as the task the machine has taken over."

questions.stem: In the carpenter example, why does judgement become more important when cutting is automated?
options: Customers trust machines less than they trust people
More cut wood exists and more of it can be misused
Machines make more mistakes than skilled carpenters
Cutting by machine takes longer than cutting by hand
questions.explanation: The second paragraph: judgement grows in importance "because there is now more cut wood in the world and more ways for it to be badly used."

questions.stem: The author suggests that the tasks machines take over first are usually those that:
options: customers value most when they buy a finished product
are easiest to describe, not those that made workers valuable
require the most physical strength and endurance
involve talking to clients about what they want
questions.explanation: The third paragraph says the tasks machines take over "are usually the ones that are easiest to describe, and those are often not the ones that made the worker valuable."

questions.stem: Which statement would the author most likely accept?
options: Every worker in an automated trade will be better off
Automation always destroys a craft within a generation
A trade may still need fewer workers after automation
Judgement can always be written down as a set of rules
questions.explanation: The last paragraph says the argument does not guarantee every worker is better off, since a trade "may need far fewer hands."

questions.stem:
The four sentences below, labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4, form a coherent paragraph when put in the right order. Decide the order and type it as a sequence of four numbers (for example, 2143).

1. It also gives the cook time to prepare the rest of the meal.

2. Many recipes ask for meat to rest for a few minutes after cooking.

3. If it is cut at once, those juices run out onto the plate.

4. Resting lets the juices settle back through the meat.
questions.explanation: Sentence 2 states the advice, 4 gives the reason, 3 shows what happens otherwise ("those juices"), and 1 adds a further benefit with "also". Order: 2431.

questions.stem:
The four sentences below, labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4, form a coherent paragraph when put in the right order. Decide the order and type it as a sequence of four numbers (for example, 2143).

1. A rumour, in this sense, is less a piece of news than a sign of what people fear.

2. Rumours spread fastest when official information is scarce.

3. People fill the gap with whatever story fits their worries.

4. The stories that travel furthest are those that confirm what listeners already suspect.
questions.explanation: Sentence 2 states when rumours spread, 3 explains how people fill the gap, 4 says which stories travel furthest, and 1 draws the conclusion "in this sense". Order: 2341.

questions.stem:
The four sentences below, labelled 1, 2, 3 and 4, form a coherent paragraph when put in the right order. Decide the order and type it as a sequence of four numbers (for example, 2143).

1. The cheaper machine, it turned out, was the more expensive choice.

2. A factory replaced its old pumps with cheaper ones to cut costs.

3. Within a year the new pumps had broken down several times.

4. Each breakdown halted production for a day and cost far more than the savings.
questions.explanation: Sentence 2 describes the decision, 3 the breakdowns, 4 their cost, and 1 gives the ironic conclusion. Order: 2341.

questions.stem:
Five sentences about a topic are given below, labelled 1 to 5. Four of them can be put together to form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not fit and type its number.

1. Desert plants have many ways of saving water.

2. Some store water in thick stems or leaves.

3. Others open their pores only at night, when the air is cooler.

4. Camels can go without drinking for long periods.

5. Many have roots that spread wide to catch rare rainfall.
questions.explanation: Sentences 1, 2, 3 and 5 list ways desert plants save water. Sentence 4 is about camels, an animal.

questions.stem:
Five sentences about a topic are given below, labelled 1 to 5. Four of them can be put together to form a coherent paragraph. Identify the sentence that does not fit and type its number.

1. A good map legend is short.

2. It explains only the symbols that actually appear on the map.

3. Readers should be able to understand it at a glance.

4. Old maps were often decorated with sea monsters.

5. A long legend sends the reader back and forth and defeats its purpose.
questions.explanation: Sentences 1, 2, 3 and 5 argue that a legend should be short and clear. Sentence 4 about decorated old maps is unrelated.

questions.stem:
The passage below is followed by four summaries. Choose the one that best captures the essence of the passage.

"Children who are praised for being clever often avoid hard tasks, because failing would threaten the label. Children praised for effort are more willing to try difficult problems, since a failure says only that they need to work harder. The kind of praise shapes the kind of risks a child will take."
options: Children should never be told that they are clever.
Clever children usually work less hard than others do.
Failure is the best teacher a child can ever have.
Praise shapes whether children attempt hard tasks.
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts praise for cleverness and for effort and concludes that "the kind of praise shapes the kind of risks a child will take."

questions.stem:
The passage below is followed by four summaries. Choose the one that best captures the essence of the passage.

"A language with no written form is not a language without rules. Its speakers follow patterns of sound and grammar as consistent as those of any written language. Writing records a language; it does not create its structure."
options: Unwritten languages are fully structured; writing only records them.
Most of the world's languages have never been written down.
Spoken languages change faster than written languages do.
Writing a language down makes its grammar more consistent.
questions.explanation: The passage says unwritten languages have consistent rules and that writing "records a language; it does not create its structure."

questions.stem:
The passage below is followed by four summaries. Choose the one that best captures the essence of the passage.

"A team that never disagrees is not necessarily a team that agrees. Its members may simply have learned that raising doubts is unwelcome. Silence of this kind hides problems until they are too large to ignore."
options: Silence can hide problems instead of showing agreement.
Teams should argue constantly so that every idea is tested.
Teams that agree on everything always make poor decisions.
Members who raise doubts are usually ignored by their leaders.
questions.explanation: The passage warns that silence may come from fear of raising doubts and so hides problems. It does not call for constant argument.

questions.stem: By what percentage did coffee exports grow from 2021 to 2024?
questions.explanation: Coffee rose from 80 to 120, an increase of 40, and 40/80 = 50%.

questions.stem: In which year did total exports rise by the most over the previous year?
options: The rise was equal every year
questions.explanation: Totals are 300, 310, 354 and 420, so the rises are 10 in 2022, 44 in 2023 and 66 in 2024.

questions.stem: By how many crore rupees did total exports rise from 2021 to 2024?
questions.explanation: Total exports were 300 in 2021 and 420 in 2024, a rise of 120.

questions.stem: What was the ratio of coffee exports to tea exports in 2023?
questions.explanation: Coffee 96 to tea 150 is 96 : 150; dividing both by 6 gives 16 : 25.

questions.stem: How many rooms in all were occupied that night?
questions.explanation: Standard 75% of 80 = 60, Deluxe 80% of 50 = 40, Suite 60% of 20 = 12, Family 90% of 30 = 27. Total 139.

questions.stem: How many rooms in the hotel were empty that night?
questions.explanation: The hotel has 80 + 50 + 20 + 30 = 180 rooms, of which 139 were occupied, leaving 41 empty.

questions.stem: Which two room types earned exactly the same room revenue that night?
options: Suite and Family
Standard and Family
Standard and Deluxe
Deluxe and Family
questions.explanation: Revenue = occupied rooms x rate: Standard 60 x 3,000 = 1,80,000; Deluxe 40 x 4,500 = 1,80,000; Suite 12 x 9,000 = 1,08,000; Family 27 x 5,000 = 1,35,000.

questions.stem: What was the room revenue from suites that night, in thousand rupees?
questions.explanation: 12 occupied suites x Rs 9,000 = Rs 1,08,000, which is 108 thousand.

questions.stem: Which box is at the top of the stack?
options: Yellow
White
Red
Blue
questions.explanation: Red and blue are a pair (blue directly on red) and green and white are a pair (white directly on green). Green is below red and yellow is above blue, so from the bottom the order is green, white, red, blue, yellow. Yellow is at the top.

questions.stem: In which position (1 to 5) is the red box?
questions.explanation: Red and blue are a pair (blue directly on red) and green and white are a pair (white directly on green). Green is below red and yellow is above blue, so from the bottom the order is green, white, red, blue, yellow. Red is third from the bottom.

questions.stem: Which box is directly below the red box?
options: Yellow
Blue
Green
White
questions.explanation: Red and blue are a pair (blue directly on red) and green and white are a pair (white directly on green). Green is below red and yellow is above blue, so from the bottom the order is green, white, red, blue, yellow. White is in position 2, directly below red.

questions.stem: How many boxes are above the white box?
questions.explanation: Red and blue are a pair (blue directly on red) and green and white are a pair (white directly on green). Green is below red and yellow is above blue, so from the bottom the order is green, white, red, blue, yellow. Red, blue and yellow are above white.

questions.stem: The cost price of 15 articles equals the selling price of 12 of them. What is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Let each article cost 1. Twelve articles sell for 15, so each sells for 15/12 = 1.25, a profit of 25%. 3/15 = 20% is the wrong base.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. If B alone finishes a job in 30 days, how many days does A take alone?
questions.explanation: A does 1.2 times B's work each day, so A needs 30/1.2 = 25 days. Taking 20% off 30 gives 24, which is wrong because time varies inversely with efficiency.

questions.stem: A 150-metre train running at 54 km/h overtakes a man walking at 6 km/h in the same direction. In how many seconds does it pass him?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 54 - 6 = 48 km/h = 48 x 5/18 = 40/3 m/s. Time = 150 / (40/3) = 11.25 s. Adding the speeds (60 km/h) gives 9 s, the time for a man walking towards the train.

questions.stem: A sum doubles itself in 5 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per year, in percent?
questions.explanation: Doubling means the interest equals the principal, 100% in 5 years, so the rate is 100/5 = 20% a year.

questions.stem: A cyclist rides from home to a market at 40 km/h and returns along the same road at 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the whole trip, in km/h?
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 x 40 x 60 / (40 + 60) = 48 km/h. The simple average, 50, is wrong because more time is spent at the slower speed.

questions.stem: The incomes of A and B are in the ratio 4 : 5 and their expenses in the ratio 3 : 4. If each saves Rs 6,000, what is A's income in rupees?
questions.explanation: Let the incomes be 4x and 5x and the expenses 3y and 4y. Then 4x - 3y = 6,000 and 5x - 4y = 6,000. Subtracting gives x = y, so 4x - 3x = 6,000 and x = 6,000. A's income is 24,000.

questions.stem: A student needs 40% of the maximum marks to pass. She scores 178 marks and fails by 22 marks. What are the maximum marks?
questions.explanation: The pass mark is 178 + 22 = 200, which is 40% of the maximum, so the maximum is 200/0.4 = 500.

questions.stem: A and B together can finish a job in 8 days, and A alone in 12 days. How many days would B alone take?
questions.explanation: B's rate = 1/8 - 1/12 = 1/24 of the job a day, so B takes 24 days. Subtracting the days, 12 - 8 = 4, has no meaning for rates.

questions.stem: If $x + \frac{1}{x} = 5$, what is $x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2}$?
If $p$ and $q$ are the roots of $x^2 - 6x + 4 = 0$, what is $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q}$?
If $f(x) = 4x - 7$, for what value of $x$ is $f(x) = 21$?
The 3rd term of a geometric progression is 12 and its 6th term is 96. What is the sum of its first 6 terms?
questions.explanation: Three steps multiply the term by 8, so the ratio is 2 and the first term is 12/4 = 3. The sum is 3 x (2^6 - 1)/(2 - 1) = 3 x 63 = 189.

questions.stem: What is the greatest value of $-x^2 + 6x + 7$?
questions.explanation: $-x^2 + 6x + 7 = 16 - (x - 3)^2$, so the greatest value is 16, at $x = 3$.

questions.stem: How many ordered pairs of positive integers $(x, y)$ satisfy $3x + 4y = 48$?
questions.explanation: $4y = 48 - 3x$, so $3x$ and therefore $x$ must be a multiple of 4: $x = 4, 8, 12$ give $y = 9, 6, 3$. $x = 16$ gives $y = 0$, which is not positive. Three pairs.

questions.stem: A father is three times as old as his son. In 12 years he will be twice as old as his son. How old is the son now, in years?
questions.explanation: Let the son be $s$: $3s + 12 = 2(s + 12)$, so $s = 12$ and the father is 36.

questions.stem: What is the sum of all values of $x$ that satisfy $|2x - 5| = 9$?
questions.explanation: $2x - 5 = 9$ gives $x = 7$ and $2x - 5 = -9$ gives $x = -2$. Their sum is 5; 7 is only the larger value.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 46 cm and a diagonal of 17 cm. What is its area in sq cm?
questions.explanation: Length + width = 23 and length^2 + width^2 = 289. Since (l + w)^2 = l^2 + w^2 + 2lw, 529 = 289 + 2lw, so lw = 120. The sides are 15 and 8.

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio 5 : 6 : 7. What is the largest angle, in degrees?
questions.explanation: The parts total 18, and the angles add up to 180 degrees, so one part is 10 degrees and the largest angle is 7 x 10 = 70.

questions.stem: What is the volume of a sphere of radius 3 cm, in cubic cm?
questions.explanation: Volume = (4/3)πr^3 = (4/3) x 27 x π = 36π. Forgetting the 1/3 gives 108π.

questions.stem: A chord 16 cm long is drawn in a circle of radius 10 cm. How far is the chord from the centre, in cm?
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, giving a right triangle with hypotenuse 10 and one side 8. The distance is the square root of 100 - 64 = 36, which is 6.

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the ratio of their areas?
questions.explanation: Areas of similar figures are in the ratio of the squares of their sides: 2^2 : 3^2 = 4 : 9. The cube ratio, 8 : 27, applies to volumes.

questions.stem: A trapezium has parallel sides of 10 cm and 16 cm and a height of 7 cm. What is its area in sq cm?
questions.explanation: Area = half the sum of the parallel sides x height = (10 + 16)/2 x 7 = 13 x 7 = 91 sq cm.

questions.stem: What is the midpoint of the segment joining (-6, 9) and (10, -3)?
questions.explanation: Average the coordinates: x = (-6 + 10)/2 = 2 and y = (9 - 3)/2 = 3. Halving the differences instead gives (8, -6).

questions.stem: A square is drawn inside a circle of radius 5 cm so that all four corners touch the circle. What is the area of the square, in sq cm?
questions.explanation: The square's diagonal is the circle's diameter, 10 cm. The area of a square is half the square of its diagonal: 100/2 = 50 sq cm.

questions.stem: How many zeros are there at the end of 100! (100 factorial)?
questions.explanation: Each trailing zero needs a factor 5. 100/5 = 20 multiples of 5 and 100/25 = 4 multiples of 25 give 20 + 4 = 24.

questions.stem: What is the smallest positive number divisible by 16, 24 and 40?
questions.explanation: $16 = 2^4$, $24 = 2^3 \times 3$ and $40 = 2^3 \times 5$, so the LCM takes the highest power of each prime: $2^4 \times 3 \times 5 = 240$.

questions.stem: In how many different ways can the letters of the word LEVEL be arranged?
questions.explanation: Five letters with L twice and E twice give 5!/(2! x 2!) = 120/4 = 30 arrangements.

questions.stem: What is the remainder when $17^{23}$ is divided by 16?
questions.explanation: 17 leaves remainder 1 on division by 16, so every power of 17 does too.

questions.stem: What is the sum of all the positive factors of 36?
questions.explanation: The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18 and 36, which add up to 91. By formula, (1 + 2 + 4)(1 + 3 + 9) = 7 x 13 = 91.

questions.stem: A fair coin is tossed four times. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
questions.explanation: The only outcome with no head is four tails, probability 1/16, so at least one head has probability 1 - 1/16 = 15/16.

questions.stem: In how many ways can 5 people stand in a row if two particular people must stand next to each other?
questions.explanation: Treat the pair as one unit: 4 units can be arranged in 4! = 24 ways, and the pair can stand in 2 orders, giving 48.

questions.stem: What is the sum of all the multiples of 3 between 1 and 100?
questions.explanation: The multiples are 3, 6, ..., 99, which is 33 terms. Their sum is 3 x (1 + 2 + ... + 33) = 3 x 561 = 1683.

questions.stem: What is the HCF of 144 and 252?
questions.explanation: $144 = 2^4 \times 3^2$ and $252 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 7$, so the HCF is $2^2 \times 3^2 = 36$.
